output.name: Halvet

anatomy.part: stern corner of the hull, the back end of the boat
keel, low in the curve of the hull's belly
bow tip, where the hull rises forward
masthead, the top of the raked mast
sail head, the peak of the sail where the gaff ends
belly of the sail, inside the bulge of the leech held full by the wind
clew, the lower back corner of the sail at the end of the boom
base of the pennant, where the streamer leaves the gaff pole
tip of the pennant, the narrow end of the tapering flag

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, a lantern boat was out past the skerries, and its crew were three women and a boy who had gone for the nets. Tavo came down on them that first night, laughing, and tore the sail to rags. The women lit their one lamp and held it up so their kin on the cliffs could find them. Orrun heard the hull groaning and lifted his back under the keel, and the boat has not sunk since. Aun saw the light and was ashamed, so he tied it to the sky, peak and boom and pennant, and Hesk counts it still. On clear nights the lantern boat sails the Leeward Reach with its sail full, and any sailor who sees it knows to turn for home. Mend your nets, the old women say. The Upper Sea is watching who comes in.
output.verse:
Halvet holds her sail
one lamp raised in the cold night
steer for home, and wait
